skill.name: firecrawl-map
skill.description: Maps a website with Firecrawl, lists discovered URLs, and optionally filters results with a search query.
skill.summary: Map website URLs with Firecrawl and filter results to find relevant pages.
skill.author: firecrawl

security_audit.summary: The static backtick, hardcoded URL, and path traversal findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline option names, and relative documentation links. The main residual risks come from the allowed npx Firecrawl command, arbitrary website mapping, and user-controlled output files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the npx Firecrawl allowance, or pin the package and version before allowing execution. Prefer a locally installed trusted Firecrawl CLI.
Require explicit user confirmation for each target domain. Do not map localhost, private IP ranges, or internal domains unless the user confirms authorization.
Constrain saved outputs to a dedicated .firecrawl directory and warn before overwriting existing files.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned npx Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The allowed tools include Bash(npx firecrawl *), which can execute package-manager managed code without a version pin. A compromised or unexpected package resolution could run unreviewed code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools block explicitly permits npx firecrawl with wildcard arguments. npx execution is a known supply-chain risk when package identity and version are not pinned.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Site Mapping Capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to map user-provided websites and can include subdomains. Without approval boundaries, it could enumerate private, internal, or unauthorized sites reachable from the runtime.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The quick-start examples and options show mapping arbitrary URLs and expanding scope to subdomains. This is intended behavior, but it needs user authorization controls.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Output Path
semantic_findings.description: The documented output option accepts a path and the examples write results to disk. Without guardrails, a user-supplied path could overwrite workspace files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file output option is documented and used in examples. The SKILL.md does not define path restrictions or overwrite safeguards.

content.value_statement: Large websites can make the right page hard to find. This skill maps URLs with Firecrawl and filters results by search terms.
actual_capabilities: Runs Firecrawl map against a user-provided website URL.
Filters discovered URLs with a search query.
Limits the number of returned URLs.
Requests structured URL results from Firecrawl.
Saves map results to an output path.
Supports sitemap handling and optional subdomain inclusion.
limitations: Requires Firecrawl CLI or npx access in the agent environment.
Mapping quality depends on site visibility, robots rules, and Firecrawl behavior.
Discovers URLs but does not scrape page contents by itself.
Output paths need care to avoid overwriting files.

use_cases.title: Find Documentation Pages
use_cases.description: Locate relevant pages on a large documentation site before reading or scraping them.

use_cases.title: Audit Site Coverage
use_cases.description: Build a URL list for a public website before planning crawl scope or content review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Content Migration
use_cases.description: Collect key URLs from an existing site before deciding which pages need export or review.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Specific Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup on a known website.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use firecrawl-map to find pages about authentication on the target documentation site. Return the most relevant URLs first.

prompt_templates.title: List Main Site URLs
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic discovery before a review task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this public website and return up to 200 discovered URLs. Group obvious documentation, pricing, and support pages.

prompt_templates.title: Search and Prepare Scrape Targets
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow that feeds a later scrape step.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the site for pages related to API keys. Identify the best pages to scrape next and explain why each page matters.

prompt_templates.title: Map With Scope Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the approved domain only, include subdomains if they match the same organization, limit results to 500 URLs, and save the list under .firecrawl.

output_examples.input: Find authentication documentation on a developer docs site.
output_examples.output: The strongest match is the API authentication guide. Related results include OAuth setup, token reference, and account security pages.

output_examples.input: Map a public marketing website before a content audit.
output_examples.output: The map found homepage, pricing, blog, documentation, support, and legal pages. The documentation section has the deepest URL set.

output_examples.input: Find pages about billing on a help center.
output_examples.output: Relevant matches include billing overview, invoice downloads, payment methods, subscription changes, and refund policy pages.

best_practices: Confirm the target domain before mapping.
Use search terms to reduce noise on large sites.
Save outputs inside a dedicated .firecrawl directory.
anti_patterns: Do not map domains without user authorization.
Do not use broad subdomain mapping unless scope is clear.
Do not save output over important project files.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It uses Firecrawl to discover URLs on a website and optionally filter them by a search query.

faq.question: Does it scrape page content?
faq.answer: No. It finds URLs. Use a scrape or crawl skill after selecting target pages.

faq.question: Can it search within a large site?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a search term so Firecrawl returns URLs that match the topic.

faq.question: Can it include subdomains?
faq.answer: Yes, when subdomain inclusion is explicitly requested and within the approved scope.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: The skill can save results to a chosen output path. A dedicated .firecrawl directory is safest.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: The agent environment needs access to Firecrawl CLI or an approved npx Firecrawl command.
